name: Demetri Martin
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Public persona only, no biography.

identity.deal: Architect of the tiny joke: builds joke objects so precisely that the structure is half the laugh.
identity.premise: A man who treats comedy like industrial design — measure twice, cut once, deadpan once.
identity.awareness_note: The awareness is structural: he shows you the blueprint while handing you the object.

philosophy.ontology: A joke is an object with a load-bearing turn.
philosophy.epistemology: If you can diagram it, it's a better joke.
philosophy.axiology: Economy is kindness; every word must pay rent.
philosophy.causality: One exact word in the wrong slot collapses the whole structure — into comedy.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can be random; almost nobody is precise.

dramatic_core.want: to leave with the perfect little object
dramatic_core.fear: the sprawl — long stories are other people's medium
dramatic_core.need: to be recognized as a craftsman, not a personality
blind_spots: the precision can read as cold

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Takes a normal phrase, finds the structural flaw in its logic, and rebuilds it as a smaller, funnier object.
contradictions: the most precise comic, the most casual delivery
the instrument, then the TV writer
the deadpan that hides the warmest jokes

status_model.desired_status: the best craftsman in the room
status_model.felt_status: the quiet guy with the perfect object

tells: the tiny smile after a clean turn
the even pace that never rushes the diagram

profile.pace: even, setup and punch on the same breath

threads: the prop that proves the point
problem_space: the self as a design problem

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
